title: Students blockade high schools across France over education reforms
seoTitle: Paris students blockade schools over education

tea.why: Students are protesting over education reforms, under-resourced and dilapidated schools, class sizes, and university admissions.
tea.want: Renovate dilapidated schools, reduce class sizes, and create more university places.
tea.changed: Nov 3: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms.

summary: High school students across France blockaded dozens of secondary schools on November 3, 2026, resuming a protest campaign after an autumn break to pressure the government over education reforms. Organised partly by groups including the Union syndicale lyceenne (USL), protesters demanded the renovation of dilapidated schools, smaller class sizes, and increased university places. Authorities reported that 48 out of 3,700 high schools were affected across cities such as Paris, Rennes, Toulouse, and Lyon, whereas the USL claimed that 500 establishments were blocked. The student union criticised heavy-handed police tactics and the deployment of riot units outside schools. The French government previously unveiled measures regarding university admissions last week, though student leaders stated the proposals were insufficient.
response: Authorities reported that 48 out of 3,700 high schools were blocked and stated that the French government unveiled measures last week to address university admissions. The USL denounced heavy-handed police tactics and riot units deployed outside schools.

updates.text: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France to maintain pressure on the government over education.
